title: AMALI: An Analytical Model for Accurately Modeling LLM Inference on Modern GPUs
problem: Existing GPU analytical models cannot accurately predict LLM inference performance because they mismodel tensor core throughput, ignore constant and instruction cache effects, and abstract away warp-level execution details critical to LLM kernels.
method: AMALI introduces three modeling innovations: (1) an instruction-modifier and throughput-based tensor core model that captures math-pipe throttle stalls by accurately modeling the pipeline fill/drain behavior of tensor cores; (2) micro-benchmark-derived analytical models for constant cache and instruction cache that measure CUDA kernel launching latencies; (3) a multi-warp model using warp instruction number distributions to reflect the heterogeneous occupancy and scheduling behavior of LLM inference kernels. All three components are validated against real A100 hardware measurements.

title: GSIM: Accelerating RTL Simulation for Large-Scale Designs
problem: Software RTL simulation is a major bottleneck in hardware design; simulation of complex processors and systems exhibits high computational overhead in multiple layers (supernode, node, and bit levels).
method: GSIM identifies and optimizes computational overhead across three levels: supernode-level optimizations for high-level logic, node-level techniques for gate-level operations, and bit-level optimizations for bitwise computation. Combines these with efficient data structures and scheduling to accelerate simulation of complex processors.

title: Einsum Trees: An Abstraction for Optimizing the Execution of Tensor Expressions
problem: Optimizing the execution of multi-operand einsum tensor expressions requires co-optimizing both the contraction path (order of binary contractions) and the data layout of intermediate tensors, but these two problems have been studied in isolation, leading to suboptimal global execution performance.
method: The paper introduces Einsum Tree IR, an intermediate representation that captures a full contraction path as a tree structure, enabling global optimization of tensor data layouts across all intermediate binary contractions simultaneously rather than locally per contraction. Given a contraction path (computed by existing algorithms), Einsum Tree IR applies global data-layout optimization to minimize data movement and improve cache utilization. The resulting optimized sequences of binary contractions are executed on general-purpose server CPUs (Arm and x86) using existing optimized BLAS/tensor kernels.

title: Chasoñ: Supporting Cross HBM Channel Data Migration to Enable Efficient Sparse Algebraic Acceleration
problem: HBM-based sparse accelerators suffer from high resource underutilization due to static non-zero scheduling that cannot redistribute work across HBM channels when data access patterns are irregular. Existing designs like Serpens fix data-to-channel mapping, leaving processing elements idle when a channel has no work.
method: Chaso is an FPGA-based streaming HBM accelerator for SpMV that introduces Cross-HBM Channel out-of-Order Scheduling (CrHCS), which dynamically migrates non-zero data across HBM channels at runtime to balance load. When one channel's processing elements are starved, CrHCS identifies data in other channels and migrates it, enabling out-of-order execution across channel boundaries. The design is implemented on AMD Alveo U55C running at 301 MHz, targeting the SuiteSparse and SNAP matrix collections.

title: Machine Learning-Guided Memory Optimization for DLRM Inference on Tiered Memory
problem: Deep learning recommendation models (DLRMs) have embedding tables at terabyte scale that cannot fit in DRAM alone; tiered memory (DRAM + cheaper capacity tiers) is cost-effective but embedding access patterns have long and irregular reuse distances that defeat classical caching and prefetching heuristics.
method: RecMG uses separate ML models for caching and prefetching of embedding vectors. The caching model predicts which vectors have long reuse distances or few future reuses and should stay in fast memory. The prefetching model uses a novel differentiable loss function to narrow the search space for candidate vectors to prefetch, minimizing on-demand fetches. Data labeling is tailored to DLRM inference characteristics (sparse accesses, variable reuse distances). Both models operate at inference time to guide real-time placement decisions on tiered memory systems.

title: UniNDP: A Unified Compilation and Simulation Tool for Near DRAM Processing Architectures
problem: Existing simulators and compilers for Near DRAM Processing (NDP) architectures are designed for specific DRAM technologies and NDP configurations, preventing cross-architecture evaluation and optimal data placement and workload scheduling for machine learning workloads.
method: UniNDP proposes a unified tree-based NDP hardware abstraction and corresponding instruction set that spans multiple DRAM technologies and NDP configurations. A cycle-accurate, instruction-driven simulator tracks working status of memory elements and processing units at fine granularity to accurately evaluate hardware performance. An NDP compiler optimizes data partition, mapping, and workload scheduling across DRAM hierarchies, using a hardware status-guided search space pruning strategy and a fast performance predictor parameterized by DRAM timing parameters to improve compilation efficiency.

title: Towards Closing the Performance Gap for Cryptographic Kernels Between CPUs and Specialized Hardware
problem: Achieving near-ASIC performance for cryptographic kernels (Number Theoretic Transform, NTT; and large-integer BLAS operations) on commodity x86 CPUs remains an open challenge; current CPU baselines lag ASICs by orders of magnitude for these workloads, which are foundational to post-quantum cryptography and fully homomorphic encryption (FHE).
method: The paper develops optimized scalar x86-64 implementations of NTT and large-integer BLAS at the per-core level, then applies SIMD vectorization using AVX2 and AVX-512 to achieve 38x and 62x speedup over state-of-the-art CPU baselines for NTT and BLAS respectively. To narrow the remaining gap, the authors propose a small x86 ISA extension called MQX (multi-word extension) that adds three new instructions targeting multi-precision modular arithmetic patterns common in NTT and BLAS. MQX cuts the slowdown relative to ASICs to as low as 35x per core; a roofline analysis of multi-core scaling shows that top-tier server CPUs with MQX can approach ASIC-level throughput.

title: FastPath: A Hybrid Approach for Efficient Hardware Security Verification
problem: Microarchitectural information leakage verification methods suffer individual weaknesses: formal methods lack scalability, simulation lacks exhaustiveness, and existing approaches have limited flexibility for changing security requirements.
method: FastPath combines simulation efficiency with formal verification exhaustiveness via a hybrid methodology that employs structural analysis to automate the verification process, enabling practical deployment in existing verification flows.

title: FF-INT8: Efficient Forward-Forward DNN Training on Edge Devices with INT8 Precision
problem: Forward-Forward (FF) algorithm replaces backpropagation's backward pass but still requires heavy memory/compute for activation storage and gradient computation; INT8 quantization for training remains unexplored despite success in inference.
method: Combines FF algorithm's layer-by-layer training with INT8 quantization to stabilize gradient computation. Proposes novel look-ahead scheme addressing FF limitations and improving accuracy. Layer-by-layer approach naturally partitions gradients for stable quantization. Evaluated on NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano (resource-constrained edge device).

title: Interleaved Logical Qubits in Atom Arrays
problem: Neutral atom quantum computers require physical qubit movement to perform two-qubit gates, which introduces an unavoidable latency bottleneck and may eliminate quantum advantage in fault-tolerant computations. Existing surface code architectures in atom arrays are movement-dependent and do not scale efficiently.
method: The paper proposes a movement-free QEC architecture based on interleaved surface code groups using dual-species neutral atom arrays. Within a group, transversal CNOTs are executed at high fidelity by leveraging asymmetric interaction strengths: interspecies interactions decay as 1/r^3 (long-range) while intraspecies decay as 1/r^6 (short-range). Between groups, interleaved lattice surgery creates high-capacity routing channels for logical qubit communication. The architecture is validated through numerical circuit simulations and benchmarked via compilation of key quantum algorithms.

title: PIMPAL: Accelerating LLM Inference on Edge Devices via In-DRAM Arithmetic Lookup
problem: Accelerating LLM inference on edge devices; General Matrix-Vector Multiplication (GEMV) is memory-intensive and difficult to accelerate with conventional edge computing; existing PIM architectures suffer from high area overhead or restricted computational precision.
method: PIMPAL processing-in-memory architecture replaces traditional arithmetic operations with parallel in-DRAM LookUp Table (LUT) based computations for GEMV. Key innovations: (1) DRAM bank subarrays divided into compute blocks for parallel LUT processing; (2) Locality-aware Compute Mapping (LCM) maximizes LUT access locality to reduce row activations; (3) LUT Aggregation (LAG) enables multi-precision via combining results from multiple small LUTs.

title: QPRAC: Towards Secure and Practical PRAC-based Rowhammer Mitigation using Priority Queues
problem: The JEDEC PRAC (Per Row Activation Counting) framework for DDR5 enables RowHammer mitigation via Alert Back-Off (ABO) signaling, but existing PRAC implementations (e.g., Panopticon) are either insecure when instantiated per JEDEC specification, or impractical (e.g., UPRAC) due to requiring oracle knowledge of the top-N most-activated rows.
method: QPRAC designs a Priority-based Service Queue (PSQ) in the memory controller that maintains pending mitigation requests sorted by row activation count, using PRAC's per-row counters to prioritize mitigations. High activation-count rows are served first, preventing adversarial bypass. The PSQ is co-designed with two complementary mechanisms: opportunistic mitigation during Refresh Management (RFM) operations (piggybacking extra mitigations at low cost), and proactive mitigation during standard DRAM refresh (REF) operations to drain the queue before ABO events fire, minimizing performance impact.

title: FRED: A Wafer-scale Fabric for 3D Parallel DNN Training
problem: Current wafer-scale interconnect topologies (e.g., 2D mesh) lack the flexibility to simultaneously support tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism in DNN training, causing collective communications to contend for shared links and inflating training time.
method: FRED introduces a distributed on-wafer topology built from tiny microswitches interconnecting accelerator chiplets on the wafer. The microswitches form a reconfigurable, nonblocking network that can route collective communications (all-reduce, all-to-all) between arbitrary subsets of chiplets without interference. In-switch collective support allows reduction operations to be partially executed at intermediate network nodes, reducing traffic volume. This topology is tailored so that different parallelism dimensions (data, tensor, pipeline) map to non-overlapping logical groups with dedicated bandwidth.

title: ZK-Hammer: Leaking Secrets from Zero-Knowledge Proofs via Rowhammer
problem: Zero-knowledge SNARK schemes are assumed cryptographically secure but their vulnerability to fault injection attacks via Rowhammer is unexplored, potentially compromising secret exponents.
method: ZK-Hammer induces Rowhammer faults into exponentiate variables in the Quadratic Arithmetic Program (QAP) representation of zk-SNARK proofs, then analyzes faulty proofs using bilinear pairing techniques to recover secret parameters.

title: STREAM: Spatiotemporal Similarity-based Efficient Approximate Median with Tunable Granularity
problem: Exact median computation is expensive and fails to meet near real-time requirements; existing approximate methods ignore spatiotemporal data characteristics and lack application-specific accuracy-speed trade-offs.
method: STREAM exploits spatiotemporal similarity in data streams to achieve bucket reuse via streaming K-means-like clustering. Introduces tunable-grained bucket mechanism allowing application-specific trade-offs between execution time and accuracy. Uses prior bucket state to accelerate median estimation.

title: Towards Secure Data Management using Multi-Cryptographic Solutions (Invited)
problem: Secure data outsourcing systems incorporate various cryptographic techniques, but their security properties are often ad hoc and obscure, making it difficult to reason about unintended information leakage.
method: Secure Normal Form (SNF) framework enabling data owners to define acceptable leakages for non-sensitive data aspects, allowing efficient query processing while guaranteeing no unintended sensitive information leakage. The paper discusses SNF application to advanced computational environments and modern data management architectures.
